note: TWO INDEPENDENT GUARDS WERE COUPLED THROUGH A SHARED STRING AND NEITHER DECLARED IT. Found while fixing the canonical heavy-tier ignore reason. cli/tests/heavy_tier.rs holds that reason as a constant and asserts every heavy-tier ignore attribute equals it VERBATIM. Separately, windows/lab/tests/preregistration_guard.rs enforces decision 0016 by requiring every ignore reason in a calibration test to name a cost OR cite a decision number - and it was recognising the heavy reason as naming a cost ONLY via the substring minutes. So deleting the word minutes, which was correct because the battery measures 4.31 s not minutes, silently broke a guard in a different crate: seven heavy-tagged ignores across disposition, health, the_fare x4 and the_mire started failing calibration_files_carry_no_unsanctioned_ignores. Nothing in either file mentions the other. The fix was to append (decision 0132) to the canonical string, which is honest because 0132 is literally the decision that renamed the target the string refers to, and which satisfies both guards by different branches of their matching logic. THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is what to carry: when guard A asserts equality against a constant and guard B pattern-matches a SUBSTRING of that same constant, the constant has two owners and one of them does not know it. Before editing any string that a test asserts verbatim, grep the string fragments - not the constant name - across the whole workspace. Caught by make gate-commit rather than by reading, which is the only reason it was caught at all.
